main.enactingFormula: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

section.heading: AUTHORITY OF STATES OF WASHINGTON, OREGON, AND CALIFORNIA TO MANAGE DUNGENESS CRAB FISHERY.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Subject to the provisions of this section and notwithstanding section 306(a) of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (16 U.S.C. 1856(a)), each of the States of Washington, Oregon, and California may adopt and enforce State laws and regulations governing fishing and processing in the exclusive economic zone adjacent to that State in any Dungeness crab (Cancer magister) fishery for which there is no fishery management plan in effect under that Act.

subsection.heading: Requirement for State Management.—
subsection.chapeau: Any law or regulation adopted by a State under this section for a Dungeness crab fishery—

paragraph.content: except as provided in paragraph (2), shall apply equally to vessels engaged in the fishery in the exclusive economic zone and vessels engaged in the fishery in the waters of the State, and without regard to the State that issued the permit under which a vessel is operating;

shall not apply to any fishing by a vessel in exercise of tribal treaty rights except as provided in United States v. Washington, D.C. No. CV–70–09213, United States District Court for the Western District of Washington; and
shall include any provisions necessary to implement tribal treaty rights pursuant to the decision in United States v. Washington, D.C. No. CV–70–09213.

subsection.heading: Limitation on Enforcement of State Limited Access Systems.—
subsection.content: Any law of the State of Washington, Oregon, or California that establishes or implements a limited access system for a Dungeness crab fishery may not be enforced against a vessel that is otherwise legally fishing in the exclusive economic zone adjacent to that State and that is not registered under the laws of that State, except a law regulating landings.

subsection.heading: State Permit or Treaty Right Required.—
subsection.content: No vessel may harvest or process Dungeness crab in the exclusive economic zone adjacent to the State of Washington, Oregon, or California, except as authorized by a permit issued by any of those States or pursuant to any tribal treaty rights to Dungeness crab pursuant to the decision in United States v. Washington, D.C. No. CV–70–09213.

subsection.heading: State Authority Otherwise Preserved.—
subsection.content: Except as expressly provided in this section, nothing in this section reduces the authority of any State under the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (16 U.S.C. 1801 et seq.) to regulate fishing, fish processing, or landing of fish.

subsection.heading: Termination of Authority.—
subsection.content: The authority of the States of Washington, Oregon, and California under this section with respect to a Dungeness crab fishery shall expire on the effective date of a fishery management plan for the fishery under the Magnuson- Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act.

subsection.heading: Repeal.—
subsection.content: Section 112(d) of Public Law 104–297 (16 U.S.C. 1856 note) is repealed.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.content: The definitions set forth in section 3 of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (16 U.S.C. 1802) shall apply to this section.

subsection.chapeau: Not later than December 31, 2001, and every 2 years thereafter, the Pacific State Marine Fisheries Commission shall submit to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate and the Committee on Resources of the House of Representatives a report on the status and management of the Dungeness Crab fishery located off the coasts of the States of Washington, Oregon, and California, including—

paragraph.content: stock status and trends throughout its range;
a description of applicable research and scientific review processes used to determine stock status and trends; and
measures implemented or planned that are designed to prevent or end overfishing in the fishery.

section.heading: SHORT TITLE.
section.content: This title may be cited as the “Hydrographic Services Improvement Act of 1998”.

paragraph.heading: Administrator.—
paragraph.content: The term “Administrator” means the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

paragraph.heading: Administration.—
paragraph.content: The term “Administration” means the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

paragraph.heading: Hydrographic data.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “hydrographic data” means information that—

footnote.p: Section 2 of Public Law 110–386 amends “[s]ection 303 of the Hydrographic Services Improvement Act of 1998 (33 U.S.C. 892) is amended by striking paragraphs (3), (4), and (5)” and inserting new paragraphs (3) through (5). The amendment was carried out to section 302 in order to reflect the probable intent of Congress.

clause.content: hydrographic, bathymetric, photogrammetric, lidar, radar, remote sensing, or shoreline and other ocean- and coastal-related surveying;
tide, water level, and current observations; or

subparagraph.content: is used in providing hydrographic services.

the management, maintenance, interpretation, certification, and dissemination of bathymetric, hydrographic, shoreline, geodetic, geospatial, geomagnetic, and tide, water level, and current information, including the production of nautical charts, nautical information databases, hydrodynamic forecast and datum transformation models, and other products derived from hydrographic data;
the development of nautical information systems; and
related activities.

paragraph.heading: Coast and geodetic survey act.—
paragraph.content: The term “Coast and Geodetic Survey Act” means the Act entitled “An Act to define the functions and duties of the Coast and Geodetic Survey, and for other purposes”, approved August 6, 1947 (33 U.S.C. 883a et seq.).

subsection.heading: Responsibilities.—
subsection.chapeau: To fulfill the data gathering and dissemination duties of the Administration under the Coast and Geodetic Survey Act, promote safe, efficient and environmentally sound marine transportation, and otherwise fulfill the purposes of this title, the Administrator shall—

paragraph.content: acquire and disseminate hydrographic data and provide hydrographic services;
promulgate standards for hydrographic data used by the Administration in providing hydrographic services;

promulgate standards for hydrographic services
provided by the Administration;
ensure comprehensive geographic coverage of hydrographic services, in cooperation with other appropriate Federal agencies;
maintain a national database of hydrographic data, in cooperation with other appropriate Federal agencies;
provide hydrographic services in uniform, easily accessible formats;

participate in the development of, and implement for the United States in cooperation with other appropriate Federal agencies, international standards for hydrographic data and hydrographic services; and
to the greatest extent practicable and cost-effective, fulfill the requirements of paragraphs (1) and (6) through contracts or other agreements with private sector entities.

subsection.heading: Authorities.—
subsection.chapeau: To fulfill the data gathering and dissemination duties of the Administration under the Coast and Geodetic Survey Act, promote precision navigation, safe, efficient, and environmentally sound marine transportation, and otherwise fulfill the purposes of this title2, subject to the availability of appropriations, the Administrator—

footnote.p: Section 7701(h)(2)(A) of division G of P.L. 119-60 provides for an amendment to strike “this Act” and insert “this title” in subsection (b) of section 303 of this Act. However “this Act” appears twice in subsection (b). Such amendment was carried out in both instances to reflect the probable intent of Congress.

paragraph.content: may procure, lease, evaluate, test, develop, and operate vessels, equipment, and technologies necessary to ensure safe navigation and maintain operational expertise in hydrographic data acquisition and hydrographic services;

shall, subject to the availability of appropriations, design, install, maintain, and operate real-time hydrographic monitoring systems and hydrodynamic forecast models to enhance navigation safety and efficiency and provide foundational information and services required to support coastal resilience planning for coastal transportation and other infrastructure, coastal protection and restoration projects, and related activities;

where appropriate and to the extent that it does not detract from the promotion of safe and efficient navigation, may acquire hydrographic data and provide hydrographic services to support the conservation and management of coastal and ocean resources;

where appropriate, may acquire hydrographic data and provide hydrographic services to save and protect life and property and support the resumption of commerce in response to emergencies, natural and man-made disasters, and homeland security and maritime domain awareness needs, including obtaining mission assignments (as defined in section 641 of the Post-Katrina Emergency Management Reform Act of 2006 (6 U.S.C. 741));
may create, support, and maintain such joint centers with other Federal agencies and other entities as the Administrator deems appropriate or necessary to carry out the purposes of this title2; and
notwithstanding the existence of such joint centers, shall award contracts for the acquisition of hydrographic data in accordance with chapter 11 of title 40, United States Code.

subsection.heading: Conservation and Management of Coastal and Ocean Resources.—
subsection.content: Where appropriate and to the extent that it does not detract from the promotion of safe and efficient navigation, the Secretary may use hydrographic data and services to support the conservation and management of coastal and ocean resources.

subsection.heading: Definition.—
subsection.content: For purposes of this section, the term “hydrographic product” means any publicly or commercially available product or service produced or disseminated by a non-Federal entity that includes or displays hydrographic data.

subparagraph.content: by not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of the Hydrographic Services Improvement Act Amendments of 2002, shall, subject to the availability of appropriations, develop and implement a quality assurance program that is equally available to all applicants, under which the Administrator may certify hydrographic products that satisfy the standards promulgated by the Administrator under section 303(a)(3) of this Act;
may authorize the use of the emblem or any trademark of the Administration on a hydrographic product certified under subparagraph (A); and
may charge a fee for such certification and use.

paragraph.heading: Limitation on fee amount.—
paragraph.content: Any fee under paragraph (1)(C) shall not exceed the costs of conducting the quality assurance testing, evaluation, or studies necessary to determine whether the hydrographic product satisfies the standards adopted under section 303(a)(3), including the cost of administering such a program.

subsection.heading: Limitation on Liability.—
subsection.content: The Government of the United States shall not be liable for any negligence by a person that produces hydrographic products certified under this section.

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.content: There is established in the Treasury a separate account, which shall be known as the “Hydrographic Services Account”.

subparagraph.content: amounts received by the United States as fees charged under subsection (b)(1)(C); and
such other amounts as may be provided by law.

paragraph.heading: Use.—
paragraph.content: Amounts in the account shall be available to the Administrator, without further appropriation, for hydrographic services.

subsection.heading: Limitation on New Fees and Increases in Existing Fees for Hydrographic Services.—
subsection.chapeau: After the date of the enactment of this Act, the Administrator may not—

paragraph.content: establish any fee or other charge for the provision of any hydrographic service except as authorized by this section; or
increase the amount of any fee or other charge for the provision of any hydrographic service except as authorized by this section and section 1307 of title 44, United States Code.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: No later than 1 year after the date of enactment of the Hydrographic Services Improvement Act Amendments of 2002, the Secretary shall establish the Hydrographic Services Review Panel.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The panel shall advise the Administrator on matters related to the responsibilities and authorities set forth in section 303 of this Act and such other appropriate matters as the Administrator refers to the panel for review and advice.

paragraph.heading: Administrative resources.—
paragraph.content: The Administrator shall make available to the panel such information, personnel, and administrative services and assistance as it may reasonably require to carry out its duties.

subparagraph.content: The panel shall consist of 15 voting members who shall be appointed by the Administrator. The Co-directors of the Center for Coastal and Ocean Mapping/Joint Hydrographic Center and no more than 2 employees of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration appointed by the Administrator shall serve as nonvoting members of the panel. The voting members of the panel shall be individuals who, by reason of knowledge, experience, or training, are especially qualified in 1 or more of the disciplines and fields relating to hydrographic data and hydrographic services, marine transportation, port administration, vessel pilotage, coastal and fishery management, and other disciplines as determined appropriate by the Administrator.
An individual may not be appointed as a voting member of the panel if the individual is a full-time officer or employee of the United States.

Any voting member of the panel who is an applicant for, or beneficiary (as determined by the Secretary) of, any assistance under this Act shall disclose to the panel that relationship, and may not vote on any matter pertaining to that assistance.

The term of office of a voting member of the panel shall be 4 years, except that of the original appointees, five shall be appointed for a term of 2 years, five shall be appointed for a term of 3 years, and five shall be appointed for a term of 4 years, as specified by the Administrator at the time of appointment.

Any individual appointed to a partial or full term may be reappointed for one additional full term. A voting member may serve after the date of the expiration of the term of office for which appointed until his or her successor has taken office.

paragraph.heading: Nominations.—
paragraph.content: At least once each year, the Secretary shall publish a notice in the Federal Register soliciting nominations for membership on the panel.

subparagraph.content: The panel shall select one voting member to serve as the Chairman and another voting member to serve as the Vice Chairman.
The Vice Chairman shall act as Chairman in the absence or incapacity of the Chairman.

subsection.heading: Compensation.—
subsection.chapeau: Voting members of the panel shall—

paragraph.content: receive compensation at a rate established by the Secretary, not to exceed the maximum daily rate payable under section 5376 of title 5, United States Code, when actually engaged in the performance of duties for such panel; and
be reimbursed for actual and reasonable expenses incurred in the performance of such duties.

subsection.heading: Meetings.—
subsection.content: The panel shall meet on a biannual basis and, at any other time, at the call of the Chairman or upon the request of a majority of the voting members or of the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Powers.—
subsection.content: The panel may exercise such powers as are reasonably necessary in order to carry out its duties under subsection (b).

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Administrator the following:

paragraph.content: To carry out nautical mapping and charting functions under sections 304 and 305, except for conducting hydrographic surveys, $71,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2023 through 2028.
To contract for hydrographic surveys under section 304(b)(1), including the leasing or time chartering of vessels,$34,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2023 through 2028.
To operate hydrographic survey vessels owned by the United States and operated by the Administration, $38,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2023 through 2028.
To carry out geodetic functions under this title, $45,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2023 through 2028.
To carry out tide and current measurement functions under this title, $35,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2023 through 2028.
To acquire a replacement hydrographic survey vessel capable of staying at sea continuously for at least 30 days $75,000,000.

subsection.heading: Arctic Programs.—
subsection.chapeau: Of the amount authorized by this section for each fiscal year—

paragraph.chapeau: $10,000,000 is authorized for use in the Arctic—

subparagraph.content: to acquire hydrographic data;
to provide hydrographic services;
to conduct coastal change analyses necessary to ensure safe navigation;
to improve the management of coastal change; and
to reduce risks of harm to subsistence and coastal communities associated with increased international maritime traffic; and

paragraph.content: $2,000,000 is authorized for use to acquire hydrographic data and provide hydrographic services in the Arctic necessary to delineate the United States extended Continental Shelf.

subsection.heading: Limitation on Administrative Expenses for Surveys.—
subsection.content: Of amounts authorized by this section for each fiscal year for contract hydrographic surveys, not more than 5 percent is authorized for administrative costs associated with contract management.

section.heading: AUTHORIZED NUMBER OF NOAA CORPS COMMISSIONED OFFICERS.

subsection.heading: Authorized Number.—
subsection.content: Amends section 2 of the Coast and Geodetic Survey Commissioned Officers' Act of 1948 (33 U.S.C. 853a).]

subsection.heading: Officer Responsible for Commissioned Officers and Vessel Fleet.—
subsection.content: Amends section 24(a) of the Coast and Geodetic Survey Commissioned Officers' Act of 1948 (33 U.S.C. 853u(a)).]

subsection.heading: Relief From Moratorium on New Appointments.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of Commerce immediately shall terminate the moratorium on new appointments of commissioned officers to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Corps.

section.heading: SHORT TITLE.
section.content: This title may be cited as the “Northwest Straits Marine Conservation Initiative Act”.

section.heading: ESTABLISHMENT.
section.content: There is established a commission to be known as the Northwest Straits Advisory Commission (in this title referred to as the “Commission”).

section.heading: ORGANIZATION AND OPERATION.
section.content: The Commission shall be organized and operated in accordance with the provisions of the Northwest Straits Citizen’s Advisory Commission Report of August 20, 1998, on file with the secretary of Commerce (in this title referred to as the “Report”).

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary of Commerce may, from amounts available to the Secretary to carry out the work of the Commission, provide assistance for use in accordance with the Report and the priorities of the Commission—

paragraph.content: to collect marine resources data in the Northwest Straits;
to coordinate Federal, State, and local marine resources protection and restoration activities in the Northwest Straits; and
to carry out other activities identified in the Report as important to the protection and restoration of marine resources in the Northwest Straits.

subsection.heading: Provision.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may provide the assistance authorized by subsection (a) through the Director of the Padilla Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve, unless the Governor of the State of Washington objects. If the Governor objects, then the Secretary may provide the assistance though the Administrator of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.

section.heading: Limitation
section.content: Nothing in this title provides the Commission with the authority to implement any Federal law or regulation.
